title: Provision and Horizon
premise: Silas Galloway, a disgraced railroad engineer hiding in the northern backcountry with a map of decommissioned lines and a debt he can never repay, is coerced into guiding a resupply mission upriver when the survey expedition he provisioned goes silent. What he finds is not disaster but a discovery the expedition's backers will burn the valley to keep: a living river route that would make their expiring concession worthless. Silas must ferry the survivors home through winter's first ice while deciding whether the map he carries becomes their salvation or their burial. In the end he burns his own closed-line map, gives the truth to the expedition's youngest member instead of the men who paid for it, and finds that the family he never meant to gather is the only asset he won't trade.
about_author: Jonah Nystrom spent a decade as a freight-line dispatcher in the boreal interior before turning to fiction, and his novels are known for their obsessive accuracy about rail, river, and cold. He writes from a cabin with no road access, reachable only when the water allows.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Silas Galloway, POV. Silas keeps his books at a fading junction depot, hiding among closed rail lines and paying down a debt to a man named Corver with quiet provisioning runs. A letter arrives: the Verrane expedition, six weeks upriver, has missed its radio window. Beat: the dread of being remembered by people he tried to forget.

chapters.title: Terms of Passage
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. Corver arrives with muscle and a contract: take a resupply crew up the Ashwater, find the expedition, tell no one what's found. Silas reads the fine print and understands he's not being hired, he's being spent. Beat: resignation sharpened into resolve; he packs the compass his father left and the map he swore to burn.

chapters.title: Crew of Strangers
chapters.summary: Silas and new POV: Junie Okafor, a nineteen-year-old radio operator who lied about her age to join. At the staging dock Silas sizes up the crew—Verrane's corporate minder Hale, two rivermen, a doctor named Brandt who seems too kind for this job. Beat: wary first bonds forming under the surface of a transaction.

chapters.title: First Water
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. The run upriver through the gorge: rapids, a near-capsize, Silas's competence earning grudging trust. Junie catches him reading the closed-lines map at night and says nothing, but files it away. Beat: the river as a test that begins stripping away pretense.

chapters.title: The Silent Camp
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. They reach the last known coordinates: camp abandoned, gear orderly, radio smashed from the inside. Hale wants to log it and turn back; Brandt insists on tracks. They find a survey stake driven into stone, marking something impossible. Beat: the shift from rescue to mystery.

chapters.title: What the Stakes Marked
chapters.summary: Junie, POV. Junie decrypts a fragment of the expedition's log: Verrane found a navigable passage through the range that would render the concession's rail monopoly worthless—and Hale's employers knew before they left. Junie tells Silas, not Hale. Beat: the first secret shared, the found-family knot beginning to tie.

chapters.title: Tracks North
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. Following the expedition's trail into the high country: a grave, freshly dug, one of the six. Brandt reads the body's story aloud with terrible gentleness. Hale quietly radios ahead against orders. Beat: grief and the growing certainty that someone in the crew is not what they seem.

chapters.title: The Living Line
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. They find the survivors—Verrane and two others—holed up in an old maintenance shelter, guarding the passage route like prisoners of their own discovery. Verrane refuses to leave without his survey plates. Beat: relief curdling into conflict; the discovery is now a hostage.

chapters.title: Hale's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Hale, POV. Hale's chapter: he calculates lives versus permits and finds the math acceptable. He sabotages the boats' fuel reserve to force the party onto the winter portage, where his company's men can intercept the plates. Beat: cold clarity; the reader now knows the trap before the heroes do.

chapters.title: The Long Portage
chapters.summary: Junie, POV. Carrying boats and plates overland through early snow, tempers fraying. Junie and Silas rig a plan: split the plates, send decoys with Hale. Brandt quietly treats Verrane's frostbite and earns his confession about what happened to the dead man. Beat: sacrifice offered freely, the first real trust.

chapters.title: Ice on the Ashwater
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. The river is freezing early; every hour of delay is a season of being stranded. Silas makes the call to run the narrowing channel at night, against every rule he's ever kept. Beat: the engineer's discipline breaking open into instinct; the price of survival begins coming due.

chapters.title: The Wreck at Sable Bend
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. One boat is lost in the ice run; a riverman drowns despite Silas's hands in the water. The crew's faith in him cracks. Hale uses the death to seize command and the remaining plates. Beat: guilt as ballast; Silas's old debt now has a new face.

chapters.title: Junie's Frequency
chapters.summary: Junie, POV. Junie, repairing the smashed expedition radio, intercepts Hale's transmission: the intercept team is already on the river below. She must choose to warn everyone and reveal she's been listening for days. She warns them. Beat: courage as confession; the crew becomes a crew.

chapters.title: Corver's Men
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. The intercept party boards at the lower rapids, led by a man Silas owes—the original debt made flesh. Corver offers Silas his freedom for the plates and the survivors' silence. Silas looks at Junie, Brandt, Verrane, and refuses for the first time in his life. Beat: the debt refused; the point of no return.

chapters.title: Running the Gap
chapters.summary: Junie, POV. A desperate escape through the gorge at first light: Silas's knowledge of the closed lines—abandoned sidings, an old trestle portage—becomes their only road. Hale, exposed, takes the plates and a boat and runs. Beat: the hunted becoming pilots of their own fate.

chapters.title: What Hale Carried
chapters.summary: Hale, POV. Hale alone on the river with the plates and a radio, discovering the plates Verrane surrendered are decoys—Junie's work. His employers' last order comes through: no witnesses. Beat: the loyalist abandoned by the ledger; even Hale begins counting differently.

chapters.title: The Trestle
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. Cornered at a collapsed trestle with winter closing in, Silas leads the party across the dead rail line he knows from his map—his father's compass in hand, his past finally useful. Hale catches up and, instead of shooting, hands over the plates and his coat. Beat: enemies converted by shared cold; the map redeemed.

chapters.title: The Concession Expires
chapters.summary: Junie, POV. They reach the junction as Corver's deadline and the concession expire together. Silas must decide: sell the route's secret to buy everyone's safety, or burn it. Verrane, broken and honest at last, tells him the valley would be dammed within a year either way. Beat: the choice distilled; survival versus truth.

chapters.title: Ash and Paper
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. Silas burns his closed-lines map and the plates together in the depot stove, keeping only one page—the passage route—folded into Junie's hand, because she's the one who'd use it for people, not permits. Corver arrives to find ash and a settled debt. Beat: the price paid in full, willingly; liberation through loss.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Brandt, POV. A tribunal over the drowned riverman and the lost expedition; Silas testifies with plain truth, taking the blame that isn't all his. The crew corroborates each other, a family under oath. Silas loses his license and keeps his name. Beat: accountability without erasure; grief given its due.

chapters.title: Provision
chapters.summary: Junie, POV. Spring: Junie, licensed now, runs supply boats on the Ashwater; Brandt stays as the valley's doctor; Verrane teaches surveying. Silas, unlicensed, becomes the man everyone trusts with the river anyway. Beat: the found family holding its shape; home built from wreckage.

chapters.title: Horizon
chapters.summary: Silas and Junie, alternating. On the first open-water run of the new season, Junie opens the folded page—the passage route—and asks what he wants to do with it. Silas says: give it to the valley. The compass needle steadies north. Beat: quiet triumph; memory kept, debt forgiven, the horizon finally open.
